findings.text: test_no_prompt_sentence_forbids_a_terminal_status_without_the_plan excludes any sentence containing 'section', and the reverted wording's own reason clause ('not whether the section closed') satisfies that exclusion, so the assertion returns an empty offenders list on exactly the regression it was added to catch; the run's own negative-control log confirms it, listing 7 failing ids and not this test. The plan's section 6 Done when names this assertion as the negative control's target, so that clause of the measure is unasserted.

_closure_block re-implements the flattened-block-up-to-the-next-FENCE shape already held by _time_fence_block at tests/test_crew_prompts.py:76; one parameterised helper would serve both, though neither is currently general.

The negative-control paragraph lists the 7 failing ids and calls the reddened test the 'plan-status assertion' without recording that the second assertion the Done when names did not redden, so a reader of the fragment alone cannot see that a declared clause of the measure is unmet.
